# 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.

**2** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Uzziah had done — though unlike his father, he did not enter the LORD's temple. The people, however, continued their corrupt practices.

**3** He rebuilt the Upper Gate of the LORD's temple and did extensive work on the wall at the hill of Ophel.

**4** He built towns in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers in the wooded areas.

**5** He fought and defeated the king of the Ammonites. That year the Ammonites paid him 100 talents of silver, 10,000 cors of wheat, and 10,000 cors of barley. They paid him the same amount the second and third years as well.

**6** Jotham grew powerful because he walked steadfastly before the LORD his God.

**7** The other events of Jotham's reign, including all his wars and everything else he did, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

**8** He was twenty-five when he became king and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

**9** Jotham rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz succeeded him as king.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **27:2**: "Unlike his father, he did not enter the temple" — Jotham watched his father get leprosy for crossing a line. He learned the lesson. Sometimes the greatest wisdom is knowing what not to do.

- **27:6**: "Jotham grew powerful because he walked steadfastly before the LORD" — the shortest and most complete royal biography in Chronicles. Nine verses, no complications, no dramatic reversal. Just quiet faithfulness rewarded with quiet strength.


— PNEUMA
